source.text: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְאַחַת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְדִידָ֥ה בַת־עֲדָ֖יָה מִבָּצְקַֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] son of eight year[s] [was] Josiah when he became king, and thirty and one year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Jedidah daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.

en.L: A son of eight years [was] Josiah when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother [was] Jedidah daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.
en.B: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.
en.R: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.

decisions.choice: a son of eight years: eight years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years (12:1; 18:2).

decisions.choice: eight years old: made king as a boy after his father was murdered
decisions.reason: Josiah's father Amon was killed by his own officials after reigning two years, and the people of the land put the eight-year-old Josiah on the throne (21:19, 23-24). The prophecy of 1 Kings 13:2 had named Josiah of the house of David long before.

decisions.choice: his mother: the queen mother named in the formula; Bozkath, a town of Judah
decisions.reason: For each king of Judah the formula names his mother, who held a place of honor at court (1 Kings 15:13; 2 Kings 18:2). Bozkath was a town in the lowland of Judah, toward Lachish (Joshua 15:39). The name Jedidah means "beloved", close to the name Jedidiah given to Solomon (2 Samuel 12:25).

decisions.choice: Josiah's reign is also told in 2 Chronicles 34-35
decisions.reason: Chronicles retells this chapter in 2 Chronicles 34:1-2 and 34:8-28, with a few differences noted at the verses where they fall.

decisions.choice: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the accession formula throughout Kings (12:1-2; 18:2). Literal keeps the Hebrew "a son of eight years" and its order; Readable says "ruled" and splits off the mother's name.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּכָל־דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔יו וְלֹא־סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and he walked in all [the] way of David his father, and not he turned aside right and left.

en.L: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and walked in all the way of David his father, and he did not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left.
en.B: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and walked in all the way of his ancestor David. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
en.R: Josiah did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right. He lived in every way as his ancestor David had lived, and he did not wander off the path, either to the right or to the left.

decisions.choice: did what was right in Yahweh's eyes: the good verdict, with no reservation
decisions.reason: This is the good verdict of the regnal formula (12:3; 18:3). No limit is added, as it was for earlier kings who left the high places standing (12:4; 15:4). Josiah is the last king of Judah to receive it, and 23:25 says that no king before or after him turned to Yahweh as he did.

decisions.choice: walked in all the way of David his father: lived as his ancestor David had lived
decisions.reason: To walk in a way is to live by a pattern of conduct. David lived more than three hundred years earlier; "father" also means a forefather, and Kings measures each king of Judah against him (1 Kings 15:3, 11; 2 Kings 18:3).

decisions.choice: did not turn aside to the right or to the left: the words Deuteronomy uses for keeping the law
decisions.reason: God's commands are pictured as a road that must not be left in either direction. Moses uses these words for all Israel (Deuteronomy 5:32; 28:14) and for the king, who is to read the law all his life and "not turn aside from the commandment, right or left" (Deuteronomy 17:18-20); Joshua is told the same (Joshua 1:7). Josiah is the king who did what Deuteronomy asks of a king.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the good verdict at each level throughout these books.

decisions.choice: his ancestor David; did not wander off the path
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestor" for "father" where David is called the father of a later king, as 18:3 does. Readable says "did not wander off the path, either to the right or to the left", the words it uses in Deuteronomy 5:32, so that the echo (m3) can be heard.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁמֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ שָׁלַ֣ח הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־שָׁפָ֨ן בֶּן־אֲצַלְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־מְשֻׁלָּם֙ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] eighteenth year of the king Josiah, sent the king Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam the scribe [to the] house of Yahweh, saying,

en.L: And it was in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe, [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying,
en.B: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent the secretary Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying,
en.R: In the eighteenth year that Josiah was king, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the royal secretary, to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He told him,

decisions.choice: the eighteenth year of King Josiah: when Josiah was about twenty-six
decisions.reason: Josiah became king at eight (verse 1), so in his eighteenth year he was about twenty-six. The book is found and the Passover kept in this same year (23:23).

decisions.choice: 2 Chronicles 34 puts Josiah's first reforms earlier
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 34:3-7 says that Josiah began to seek God in his eighth year and to purge Judah and Jerusalem of idols in his twelfth, before the book was found. Kings tells the whole reform after the finding of the book (chapter 23). 2 Chronicles 34:8 adds that Maaseiah the governor of the city and Joah the recorder were sent with Shaphan.

decisions.choice: Shaphan the scribe: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: The scribe was one of the king's chief officials, who kept records and handled royal business (12:11; 18:18). Shaphan and his sons appear again in verse 12 and in Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:24; 36:10-12).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 4
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the king's orders, which run from verse 4 to the end of verse 7.

decisions.choice: the scribe (Literal); the secretary (Balanced); the royal secretary (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 12:11, Balanced and Readable name the office by its modern equivalent; Literal keeps "scribe". Readable says "temple" for "house of the LORD", as these books do.

source.text: עֲלֵ֗ה אֶל־חִלְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל וְיַתֵּ֣ם אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף הַמּוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָסְפ֛וּ שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּ֖ף מֵאֵ֥ת הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Go up to Hilkiah the priest the great, and let him complete the money brought [into the] house of Yahweh, which have gathered [the] keepers of the threshold from the people,

en.L: "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, and let him complete the money that has been brought [into the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered from the people,
en.B: "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and have him count up the money brought into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the money the doorkeepers have taken in from the people,
en.R: "Go to Hilkiah the high priest. Have him count the money that people have brought to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The men who guard the entrance have collected it from the people.

decisions.choice: let him complete the money: have him count it up, reckon the total
alternatives: let him melt down the money
decisions.reason: The verb means to complete or finish, and here most likely to make up the full sum, counting out what had come in. Some read a very similar verb meaning to pour out or melt down, the word Shaphan uses in verse 9, but the written text has "complete".

decisions.choice: the keepers of the threshold: the priests who guarded the temple entrance
decisions.reason: These are the doorkeepers who received the people's gifts at the entrance and put them in the chest that Jehoash had set up (12:10). Josiah uses the arrangement made for the repairs under Jehoash (12:10-16).

decisions.choice: Hilkiah the high priest
decisions.reason: Literally "the great priest", the title of the chief priest (12:11; Leviticus 21:10). Hilkiah is named among the ancestors of Ezra (Ezra 7:1; 1 Chronicles 5:39).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 5
decisions.reason: The king's orders form one long sentence from here to the end of verse 6: count the money, hand it to the overseers, and have them pay the workmen.

decisions.choice: doorkeepers (Balanced); the men who guard the entrance (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the duty that "keepers of the threshold" stands for, as at 12:10; Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: וְיִתְּנֻ֗הוּ עַל־יַד֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה הַמֻּפְקָדִ֖ים בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְיִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ לְעֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְחַזֵּ֖ק בֶּ֥דֶק הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: and let them give it on [the] hand of [the] doers of the work, those appointed [in the] house of Yahweh; and let them give it to [the] doers of the work who [are] in [the] house of Yahweh, to repair [the] breach of the house,

en.L: and let them give it into [the] hand of the doers of the work, who are appointed in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and let them give it to the doers of the work who [are] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to repair the breach of the house,
en.B: and have them hand it to the men doing the work, who have been put in charge of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let these pay it to the workmen in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who are repairing the damage to the house,
en.R: Then have them give it to the men who have been put in charge of the work on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. These men are to pay the workers who are repairing the temple.

decisions.choice: let them give it ... the house: the readings in the margin
decisions.reason: In two places the letters written in the Hebrew text differ slightly from the reading given in the margin: in the form of "let them give it", and where the margin reads "in the house" for "the house". The record follows the margin; the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the doers of the work: first the overseers, then the workmen they pay
decisions.reason: The phrase is used twice. The first time it names the men appointed over the work, who receive the money; the second time it names the workmen in the temple whom they pay, listed in verse 6. 12:12 has the same two steps.

decisions.choice: to repair the breach of the house: the words of the repairs under Jehoash
decisions.reason: The words follow 12:6, 12 and 15 closely. The temple, built some three hundred and fifty years earlier, needed repair again after the long reign of Manasseh, who had set up altars to other gods in its courts (21:4-5).

decisions.choice: the breach of the house (Literal); the damage to the house (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The same wording as in 12:6 and 12:12, where the Hebrew is the same. Readable says "repairing the temple".

source.text: לֶחָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְלַבֹּנִ֖ים וְלַגֹּֽדְרִ֑ים וְלִקְנ֤וֹת עֵצִים֙ וְאַבְנֵ֣י מַחְצֵ֔ב לְחַזֵּ֖ק אֶת־הַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: to the craftsmen and to the builders and to the masons, and to buy timber and stones of hewing to repair the house.

en.L: to the craftsmen and to the builders and to the masons, and to buy timber and hewn stones to repair the house.
en.B: to the craftsmen, the builders and the masons, and let them buy timber and dressed stone to repair the house.
en.R: These are the craftsmen, the builders and the masons. They are also to buy wood and cut stone to repair the temple.

decisions.choice: craftsmen, builders and masons: the workmen paid with the money
decisions.reason: The first word means skilled workers in wood, stone or metal; in 12:12 they are called craftsmen of wood. The last word is from a verb meaning to build a wall, as in 12:13: the men who laid the stone.

decisions.choice: timber and hewn stones: as in 12:13
decisions.reason: The same materials were bought for the repairs under Jehoash (12:13): wood and stone cut and shaped at the quarry (1 Kings 5:31).

decisions.choice: craftsmen; hewn stones (Literal); dressed stone (Balanced); cut stone (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 12:13 where the Hebrew is the same. Readable makes the list its own sentence and closes the king's orders with "They are also to buy".

source.text: אַ֚ךְ לֹא־יֵחָשֵׁ֣ב אִתָּ֔ם הַכֶּ֖סֶף הַנִּתָּ֣ן עַל־יָדָ֑ם כִּ֥י בֶאֱמוּנָ֖ה הֵ֥ם עֹשִֽׂים׃

records.literal_gloss: Only not will be reckoned with them the money given on their hand, for in faithfulness they [are] acting.

en.L: Only, the money that is given into their hand shall not be reckoned with them, for they act in faithfulness."
en.B: But no accounting is to be asked of them for the money handed to them, because they deal honestly."
en.R: Do not ask them to give an account of the money they receive, because they are honest."

decisions.choice: they act in faithfulness: the words said of the overseers under Jehoash
decisions.reason: 12:16 says the same of the men who paid the workmen in Jehoash's day: no one checked their accounts, "for they acted in faithfulness". Here the words are part of the king's orders.

decisions.choice: not reckoned with them ... in faithfulness: no accounts asked, because they are honest
decisions.reason: The verb means to count or reckon, here to call for an account of how money was spent. The noun means steadiness and reliability: these men could be trusted with the money.

decisions.choice: the king's orders end here
decisions.reason: The verse is still part of what the king tells Shaphan to say. "Them" are the overseers who receive the money (verse 5).

decisions.choice: they act in faithfulness / they deal honestly / they are honest
decisions.reason: The wording of 12:16 at each level, in the present tense because here it is the king speaking.

source.text: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר חִלְקִיָּ֜הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֤ן הַגָּדוֹל֙ עַל־שָׁפָ֣ן הַסֹּפֵ֔ר סֵ֧פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֛ה מָצָ֖אתִי בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֨ן חִלְקִיָּ֧ה אֶת־הַסֵּ֛פֶר אֶל־שָׁפָ֖ן וַיִּקְרָאֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Hilkiah the priest the great to Shaphan the scribe, [the] book of the law I have found in [the] house of Yahweh; and gave Hilkiah the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

en.L: And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "The book of the law I have found in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
en.B: Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "In the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I have found the book of the law." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
en.R: Hilkiah the high priest told Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} teaching in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." He gave the book to Shaphan, and Shaphan read it.

decisions.choice: the book of the law: the book of Yahweh's instruction
decisions.reason: The word for "law" (torah) means instruction or teaching, the whole of what Yahweh taught through Moses, not only rules (Deuteronomy 1:5; 31:9). 2 Chronicles 34:14 calls it "the book of the law of Yahweh given through Moses".

decisions.choice: the book is usually identified with Deuteronomy, or its core
alternatives: a part of Deuteronomy, such as chapters 12-26 and 28
decisions.reason: The book is not named further, but what it leads Josiah to do matches Deuteronomy closely: worship at one place only (23:8-9; Deuteronomy 12), the removal of mediums and of sacred pillars and poles (23:14, 24; Deuteronomy 16:21-22; 18:10-11), the Passover kept at the chosen place (23:21-23; Deuteronomy 16:1-8) and the curses that alarm the king (verses 11-13; Deuteronomy 28). Deuteronomy itself calls itself "this book of the law" and was to be kept beside the ark (Deuteronomy 31:24-26). It may also have been the whole five books of Moses or a part of Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: I have found the book: a scroll that had been lost or neglected
decisions.reason: A "book" was a scroll. The text does not say how it came to be lost; under Manasseh and Amon the temple had been given over to other gods for some fifty-five years (21:1-7, 19-22), and the scroll may have lain unused, or come to light during the repairs.

decisions.choice: the book of the LORD's teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for torah, as in Deuteronomy, because "law" alone makes most readers think only of rules (m1). It adds whose teaching it is, as 2 Chronicles 34:14 does, so the reader does not take it for a book of human laws. Literal and Balanced keep "the book of the law".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֞א שָׁפָ֤ן הַסֹּפֵר֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִתִּ֤יכוּ עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ הַנִּמְצָ֣א בַבַּ֔יִת וַֽיִּתְּנֻ֗הוּ עַל־יַד֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה הַמֻּפְקָדִ֖ים בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Shaphan the scribe to the king, and he brought back [to] the king word, and he said, have poured out your servants the money found in the house, and they have given it on [the] hand of [the] doers of the work, those appointed [in the] house of Yahweh.

en.L: And Shaphan the scribe came to the king, and brought back word to the king, and he said, "Your servants have poured out the money that was found in the house, and they have given it into [the] hand of the doers of the work, who are appointed in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Shaphan the secretary went to the king and reported to him, "Your officials have emptied out the money found in the house and handed it over to the men doing the work, who have been put in charge of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Shaphan the secretary went to the king and reported, "Your officials have emptied out the money that was found in the temple. They have given it to the men in charge of the work on the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: poured out the money: emptied the chest
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out. Here it most likely means that the officials emptied the money out of the chest (12:10-11) to be weighed and paid out. The same verb is used of melting metal in a furnace (Ezekiel 22:20-22), so it may mean that the silver was melted down into bars.

decisions.choice: brought back word to the king: reported to him
decisions.reason: To bring back a word is to give a report on a task one was sent to do. Shaphan reports the money first; only then does he speak of the book (verse 10).

decisions.choice: your servants: the king's officials who handled the money
decisions.reason: Shaphan speaks of the men who carried out the king's order as the king's servants, his officials, not household slaves.

decisions.choice: your officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are "officials" at Balanced and Readable, as throughout these books; Literal keeps "servants".

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֞ד שָׁפָ֤ן הַסֹּפֵר֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר סֵ֚פֶר נָ֣תַן לִ֔י חִלְקִיָּ֖ה הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַיִּקְרָאֵ֥הוּ שָׁפָ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And told Shaphan the scribe to the king, saying, [a] book has given to me Hilkiah the priest; and read it Shaphan before the king.

en.L: And Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, "A book Hilkiah the priest has given me." And Shaphan read it before the king.
en.B: Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has handed me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud to the king.
en.R: Shaphan the secretary also told the king, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." Then he read it aloud to the king.

decisions.choice: a book: Shaphan names it without saying what it is
decisions.reason: "A book" stands first in Shaphan's words. He does not repeat Hilkiah's words "the book of the law" (verse 8); the king learns what it is by hearing it read.

decisions.choice: read it before the king: read it aloud to him
decisions.reason: Reading was usually done aloud, and to read "before" someone is to read in his hearing (Deuteronomy 31:11). 2 Chronicles 34:18 says that Shaphan "read in it", which may mean he read parts of it.

decisions.choice: aloud
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "aloud" for what reading "before the king" means (m2).

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֖י סֵ֣פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when heard the king the words of [the] book of the law, and he tore his clothes.

en.L: And it was, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his clothes.
en.B: When the king heard the words written in the book of the law, he tore his clothes.
en.R: When the king heard the words of the book of {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} teaching, he tore his clothes in grief.

decisions.choice: he tore his clothes: a sign of grief and alarm
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes was the outward sign of grief, dismay or repentance (18:37; 19:1; 1 Kings 21:27). The king sees that the words of the book stand against his people (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the words of the book of the law: what was written in it
decisions.reason: The narrator now names the book as Hilkiah did (verse 8). The words are its commands and its warnings (verse 13).

decisions.choice: in grief (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in grief" to say what tearing the clothes meant (m1). It says "the book of the LORD's teaching" as in verse 8.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־חִלְקִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֡ן וְאֶת־אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־שָׁ֠פָן וְאֶת־עַכְבּ֨וֹר בֶּן־מִיכָיָ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת׀שָׁפָ֣ן הַסֹּפֵ֗ר וְאֵ֛ת עֲשָׂיָ֥ה עֶֽבֶד־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Achbor son of Micaiah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah [the] servant of the king, saying,

en.L: And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Achbor son of Micaiah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,
en.B: Then the king gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king's official,
en.R: Then the king gave an order to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah, an official of the king. He said,

decisions.choice: Ahikam son of Shaphan; Achbor son of Micaiah
decisions.reason: Ahikam was the son of Shaphan the secretary. He later protected the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 26:24), and his son Gedaliah was made governor of Judah after the fall of Jerusalem (25:22). Achbor's son Elnathan was one of the officials under Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 26:22; 36:12).

decisions.choice: Achbor son of Micaiah: called Abdon son of Micah in Chronicles
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 34:20 names him Abdon son of Micah. Micah is a short form of Micaiah; the two forms of the first name may come from different ways of writing it down.

decisions.choice: Asaiah the servant of the king: a title for a royal official
decisions.reason: "Servant of the king" was the title of a high officer serving the king directly, not a household slave (25:8 uses the same words of a Babylonian officer).

decisions.choice: the sentence goes on into verse 13
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the king's command, given in verse 13.

decisions.choice: the king's official (Balanced); an official of the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servant is an "official" at Balanced and Readable, as throughout these books; Literal keeps "servant".

source.text: לְכוּ֩ דִרְשׁ֨וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֜ה בַּעֲדִ֣י וּבְעַד־הָעָ֗ם וּבְעַד֙ כָּל־יְהוּדָ֔ה עַל־דִּבְרֵ֛י הַסֵּ֥פֶר הַנִּמְצָ֖א הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־גְדוֹלָ֞ה חֲמַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הִיא֙ נִצְּתָ֣ה בָ֔נוּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֜וּ אֲבֹתֵ֗ינוּ עַל־דִּבְרֵי֙ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כְּכָל־הַכָּת֥וּב עָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Go, inquire of Yahweh for me and for the people and for all Judah concerning [the] words of the book the found the this; for great [is] [the] wrath of Yahweh which it has been kindled against us, because that not listened our fathers to [the] words of the book the this, to do according to all the written concerning us.

en.L: "Go, inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for me and for the people and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great [is] the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written concerning us."
en.B: "Go and ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on my behalf, and on behalf of the people and all Judah, about the words of this book that has been found. {{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} anger burns hot against us, because our ancestors did not listen to the words of this book or do all that it lays down for us."
en.R: "Go and ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the words of this book that has been found. Ask for me, for the people and for all Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is very angry with us, because our ancestors did not obey the words of this book. They did not do what it tells us to do."

decisions.choice: inquire of Yahweh: seek a word from Yahweh through a prophet
decisions.reason: To "seek" Yahweh in this sense is to ask for his answer on a matter, usually through a prophet (1 Kings 22:7-8; 2 Kings 3:11). The officials go to Huldah (verse 14).

decisions.choice: great is the wrath of Yahweh that has been kindled: his anger burns
decisions.reason: The noun is a strong word for burning anger, and the verb pictures it set alight like a fire. Huldah's answer takes up the same picture (verse 17).

decisions.choice: all that is written concerning us: what the book lays on us
decisions.reason: The words can mean what the book requires of Israel, or what it writes against them, its curses (Deuteronomy 28:15-68). The king fears both: the commands were not kept, and so the curses stand.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", the generations before; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: the people for whom they ask placed in a second sentence (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long command into short sentences and says "obey" for "listen to", the sense the verb has with a command.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַ֠כֹּהֵן וַאֲחִיקָ֨ם וְעַכְבּ֜וֹר וְשָׁפָ֣ן וַעֲשָׂיָ֗ה אֶל־חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה אֵ֣שֶׁת׀שַׁלֻּ֣ם בֶּן־תִּקְוָ֗ה בֶּן־חַרְחַס֙ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַבְּגָדִ֔ים וְהִ֛יא יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וַֽיְדַבְּר֖וּ אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah to Huldah the prophetess, [the] wife of Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas, keeper of the garments, and she [was] living in Jerusalem in the Second [Quarter]; and they spoke to her.

en.L: And Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments; and she [was] living in Jerusalem in the Second [Quarter]; and they spoke to her.
en.B: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan and Asaiah went to the prophet Huldah, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. Her home was in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem, and they spoke with her.
en.R: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan and Asaiah went to speak with Huldah. She was a prophet. Her husband was Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, the man in charge of the wardrobe. She lived in the newer part of Jerusalem called the Second Quarter.

decisions.choice: Huldah the prophetess: a woman who spoke Yahweh's word
decisions.reason: The noun is the feminine form of the word for "prophet", used also of Miriam (Exodus 15:20) and Deborah (Judges 4:4). The king's officials, the high priest among them, go to her for Yahweh's answer.

decisions.choice: keeper of the garments: in charge of a wardrobe, royal or priestly
decisions.reason: Shallum looked after a store of clothing. It may have been the king's wardrobe or the vestments kept for the temple (10:22 speaks of the one in charge of the vestments in the temple of Baal); the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the Second Quarter: a newer district of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means "second" or "double". Here it most likely names a part of the city added later, outside the oldest walls, probably on the western hill (Zephaniah 1:11; Nehemiah 11:9 speaks of one "second over the city"). Where exactly it lay is not certain; an older understanding took it to mean a school or college.

decisions.choice: Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas: named a little differently in Chronicles
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 34:22 names Huldah's husband Shallum son of Tokhath son of Hasrah. The names are close in form and most likely spellings of the same names.

decisions.choice: the prophet (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: English now uses "prophet" for women and men alike, as at Judges 4:4; Literal keeps "prophetess". "Wardrobe" at Balanced and Readable names what "the garments" are.

decisions.choice: the newer part of the city called the Second Quarter (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the district's name (m3) and splits the description into short sentences.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִמְר֣וּ לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to them, thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, say to the man who sent you to me,

en.L: And she said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
en.B: She said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the man who sent you to me,
en.R: She told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Give this message to the man who sent you to me,

decisions.choice: thus says Yahweh: the messenger's formula
decisions.reason: A messenger began by naming the one whose words he carried. Prophets use the formula to show that what follows is Yahweh's word, not their own.

decisions.choice: the man who sent you: Huldah speaks of the king simply as "the man"
decisions.reason: Before Yahweh's sentence on Judah, the king is "the man who sent you". When the word turns to Josiah himself, she calls him "the king of Judah" (verse 18).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the formula at each level in these books. Huldah's answer opens with a double quote mark here and closes at the end of her last words in verse 20; the message for the king opens with a single quote mark in verses 16 and 18.

source.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְעַל־יֹֽשְׁבָ֑יו אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָרָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, here I [am] bringing evil to the place the this and on its inhabitants, all [the] words of the book which has read [the] king of Judah;

en.L: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] bringing evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read,
en.B: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to bring disaster on this place and on those who live in it, all the words in the book the king of Judah has read,
en.R: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to bring disaster on this place and on the people who live here. Everything written in the book that the king of Judah has read will happen.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm brought as punishment
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means evil done or evil suffered. Here it is the disaster Yahweh brings as judgment, not wrongdoing (1 Kings 14:10; 21:21).

decisions.choice: all the words of the book: the disaster is what the book threatens
decisions.reason: "All the words of the book" stands beside "evil" and says what it is: the curses written in the book will now fall (Deuteronomy 28:15-68; 29:19-27). "This place" is Jerusalem and Judah.

decisions.choice: look, I am bringing: about to happen
decisions.reason: The word "look" with the participle announces something that is sure and near.

decisions.choice: disaster (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:10, Balanced and Readable say "disaster" for the harm Yahweh brings (m1); Literal keeps "evil".

decisions.choice: everything written in the book ... will happen (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the words of the book a sentence of their own and supplies "will happen" to show how they belong to the disaster (m2).

source.text: תַּ֣חַת׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲזָב֗וּנִי וַֽיְקַטְּרוּ֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְמַ֨עַן֙ הַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי בְּכֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיהֶ֑ם וְנִצְּתָ֧ה חֲמָתִ֛י בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: because that they have forsaken me and they have burned incense to gods other, so as to provoke me to anger with all [the] work of their hands; and will be kindled my wrath against the place the this, and not it will be quenched.

en.L: because they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and have burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with all the work of their hands; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will be kindled against this place, and it will not be quenched.'
en.B: because they have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and burned incense to other gods, provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with all the work of their hands. So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will blaze against this place, and it will not be put out.'
en.R: This will happen because they have left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and burned incense to other gods. They have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with all the idols they have made with their hands. So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will burn against this place like a fire that no one can put out.'

decisions.choice: burned incense: or made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, of incense or of offerings burned on an altar (12:4).

decisions.choice: provoke me to anger with the work of their hands: the words of Deuteronomy
alternatives: by all that they have done
decisions.reason: Moses warned that Israel would do evil and provoke Yahweh "with the work of your hands" (Deuteronomy 31:29; 4:28). The work of their hands is the idols they made, and may take in all their deeds.

decisions.choice: my wrath will be kindled ... will not be quenched: the judgment will not be turned back
decisions.reason: Yahweh's anger is pictured as a fire, as the king had said (verse 13). A fire that will not be put out means a sentence that will not be withdrawn (Jeremiah 7:20). 23:26-27 says that even Josiah's reform did not turn it back.

decisions.choice: abandoned (Balanced); left (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use common words for "forsaken". Readable adds "This will happen" to tie the reason to verse 16.

decisions.choice: like a fire that no one can put out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "like a fire" so that the picture in "will not be quenched" is plain (m3).

source.text: וְאֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְכֶם֙ לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלָ֑יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] king of Judah who sent you to inquire of Yahweh, thus you shall say to him, thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, the words which you have heard,

en.L: And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, thus you shall say to him: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: [As for] the words that you have heard,
en.B: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, say this: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: As for the words you have heard,
en.R: But say this to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} about the book: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says about the words you have heard:

decisions.choice: the words that you have heard: the sentence breaks off
decisions.reason: The phrase stands alone and is not finished; the sentence starts again in verse 19 with "because". It means "as for the words you have heard", the words of the book.

decisions.choice: the king of Judah: now named by his office
decisions.reason: In verse 15 Huldah called him "the man who sent you". Now the word is for Josiah himself, and she names him as king.

decisions.choice: to inquire of Yahweh: as in verse 13
decisions.reason: To seek Yahweh's answer through a prophet.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: As in verse 15. A single quote mark opens the message for the king.

source.text: יַ֠עַן רַךְ־לְבָ֨בְךָ֜ וַתִּכָּנַ֣ע׀מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּֽשָׁמְעֲךָ֡ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּרְתִּי֩ עַל־הַמָּק֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה וְעַל־יֹשְׁבָ֗יו לִהְי֤וֹת לְשַׁמָּה֙ וְלִקְלָלָ֔ה וַתִּקְרַע֙ אֶת־בְּגָדֶ֔יךָ וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: because was soft your heart, and you humbled yourself before Yahweh when you heard what I spoke against the place the this and against its inhabitants, to become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your clothes and you wept before me, and also I have heard, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: because your heart was soft and you humbled yourself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they would become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I also have heard, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: because your heart was tender, and when you heard what I spoke against this place and its people, that they would become a horror and a curse, you humbled yourself before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and because you tore your clothes and wept before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I in turn have heard you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: When you heard what I said against this place and the people who live here, that it would become a ruin and a name people would use when they curse, your heart was moved and you made yourself humble before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You tore your clothes and wept in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence. So I have listened to you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your heart was soft: you were open and responsive, not hardened
decisions.reason: A soft heart takes a warning to heart and is moved by it; a hard heart refuses (Deuteronomy 2:30; 2 Chronicles 36:13).

decisions.choice: a desolation and a curse: a ruin that appalls, and a name used in curses
decisions.reason: The first word means a waste that makes those who see it shudder; the second means that the place would become a byword, its name used when people curse (Deuteronomy 28:37; Jeremiah 24:9).

decisions.choice: you humbled yourself ... and wept before me: Yahweh answers repentance
decisions.reason: As with Ahab, who humbled himself when he heard Elijah's words (1 Kings 21:27-29), Yahweh takes note of Josiah's grief. The judgment on Judah is not withdrawn (verse 17), but it is put off beyond his lifetime (verse 20).

decisions.choice: I also have heard: Yahweh has heard the king
decisions.reason: "I" is emphatic: as Josiah heard Yahweh's words, Yahweh in turn has heard him. "Declares Yahweh" seals the promise.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this phrase in these books.

decisions.choice: your heart was moved; a ruin, and a name people would use when they curse (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom (m1) and of the two nouns (m2), and splits the long sentence into short ones.

source.text: לָכֵן֩ הִנְנִ֨י אֹֽסִפְךָ֜ עַל־אֲבֹתֶ֗יךָ וְנֶאֱסַפְתָּ֣ אֶל־קִבְרֹתֶיךָ֮ בְּשָׁלוֹם֒ וְלֹא־תִרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹל֙ הָֽרָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י מֵבִ֖יא עַל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore here I [am] gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your graves in peace, and not will look your eyes on all the evil which I [am] bringing on the place the this. And they brought back [to] the king word.

en.L: Therefore, look, I [am] gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your graves in peace, and your eyes will not look on all the evil that I [am] bringing on this place.'" And they brought back word to the king.
en.B: Therefore I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. You will not see with your own eyes all the disaster I am going to bring on this place.'" Then they took her answer back to the king.
en.R: So I will let you die and join your ancestors. You will be buried in peace, and you will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place.'" Then the men took her answer back to the king.

decisions.choice: gather you to your fathers ... gathered to your grave: you will die and be buried with your ancestors
decisions.reason: To be gathered to one's fathers is to die and join those who have died before (Judges 2:10). "Graves" is plural, most likely the family tomb where the kings of Judah were buried.

decisions.choice: in peace: before the disaster, and buried in his own tomb
alternatives: a promise of a peaceful death, which Josiah forfeited
decisions.reason: Josiah was killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Neco (23:29-30), so "in peace" does not mean a peaceful death. The verse explains it: his eyes would not see the disaster Yahweh would bring on Jerusalem. He died while Judah still stood and was buried in his own tomb (23:30). Some read the promise as one Josiah lost by going out against Neco against God's warning (2 Chronicles 35:21-22).

decisions.choice: they brought back word to the king: the officials report
decisions.reason: Huldah's answer ends with the words of Yahweh; the officials take it back to Josiah, and chapter 23 tells what he did.

decisions.choice: gathered to your grave (Balanced); buried (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of being gathered, which echoes the first half of the verse; Readable says plainly what it means. "Ancestors" for "fathers" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: I will let you die and join your ancestors (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the idiom (m1).
